question: All of the following side effects are produced by Cisplatin except
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cisplatin" -> "neurotoxic effects continue after treatment stops" -> "Coasting effect" -> 90%
analysis: Cisplatin, a chemotherapy drug, is well-documented to cause several side effects due to its cytotoxic effects on various cells and tissues. Among the listed options, ototoxicity (damage to the ear causing hearing loss) and nephrotoxicity (damage to the kidneys) are well-established side effects of Cisplatin. These effects are due to the accumulation of the drug in the inner ear hair cells and renal tubular cells, respectively. The coasting effect, where neurotoxic effects continue even after the cessation of treatment, is also a recognized phenomenon associated with Cisplatin. However, pulmonary fibrosis, which involves scarring and damage to lung tissue, is not typically associated with Cisplatin use. This aligns with the medical consensus and available literature, which do not link Cisplatin with pulmonary fibrosis as a side effect. Therefore, the most likely correct answer, based on known medical facts and consensus, is that pulmonary fibrosis is not a side effect produced by Cisplatin.
